Since we know there are 6 edges and U has no parents, let's use constraint-based approach\n# First, let's compute pairwise mutual information to understand relationships\ndef compute_mutual_info_matrix(data):\n    \"\"\"Compute pairwise mutual information matrix\"\"\"\n    cols = data.columns\n    n_cols = len(cols)\n    mi_matrix = np.zeros((n_cols, n_cols))\n    \n    for i in range(n_cols):\n        for j in range(i+1, n_cols):\n            mi = mutual_info_regression(data[[cols[i]]], data[cols[j]])[0]\n            mi_matrix[i, j] = mi\n            mi_matrix[j, i] = mi\n    \n    return pd.DataFrame(mi_matrix, index=cols, columns=cols)\n\nprint(\"\\nComputing mutual information matrix...\")\nmi_matrix = compute_mutual_info_matrix(df)\nprint(\"Mutual Information Matrix:\")\nprint(mi_matrix)\n\n# Let's also check correlations\nprint(\"\\nCorrelation Matrix:\")\ncorr_matrix = df.corr()\nprint(corr_matrix)\n\n# Using PC algorithm for structure learning\nprint(\"\\nApplying PC algorithm for structure learning...\")\npc = PC(df)\ndag_pc = pc.estimate(variant=\"stable\", max_cond_vars=2, return_type=\"dag\")\nprint(f\"PC Estimated edges: {dag_pc.edges()}\")\n\n# Let's also try Hill Climbing with BIC score\nprint(\"\\nApplying Hill Climbing with BIC scoring...\")\nhc = HillClimbSearch(df)\nbest_model = hc.estimate(scoring_method=BicScore(df), max_indegree=3, max_iter=1000)\nprint(f\"Hill Climbing estimated edges: {best_model.edges()}\")\n\n# Apply constraints: U has no parents and there are exactly 6 edges\n# We need to manually adjust the structure based on the constraints\n\n# First, let's count edges in both models\npc_edges = list(dag_pc.edges())\nhc_edges = list(best_model.edges())\n\nprint(f\"PC edges count: {len(pc_edges)}\")\nprint(f\"Hill Climbing edges count: {len(hc_edges)}\")\n\n# Based on constraint that U has no parents, let's filter edges pointing to U\npc_edges_filtered = [(u, v) for u, v in pc_edges if v != 'U']\nhc_edges_filtered = [(u, v) for u, v in hc_edges if v != 'U']\n\nprint(f\"PC edges after filtering U as child: {pc_edges_filtered}\")\nprint(f\"Hill Climbing edges after filtering U as child: {hc_edges_filtered}\")\n\n# Adjust to exactly 6 edges if needed\n# If we have more than 6 edges, remove the ones with weakest relationships\n# If we have fewer than 6 edges, add plausible ones\n\n# Let's use a combination of both approaches and domain knowledge\n# Since we know there should be 6 edges and U has no parents, let's construct our DAG\n\n# First let's check if either method gives us exactly 6 edges with U having no parents\nif len(pc_edges_filtered) == 6:\n    final_edges = pc_edges_filtered\n    print(\"Using PC algorithm result\")\nelif len(hc_edges_filtered) == 6:\n    final_edges = hc_edges_filtered\n    print(\"Using Hill Climbing result\")\nelse:\n    # Need to manually adjust to 6 edges\n    print(\"Manually adjusting to 6 edges with constraint that U has no parents\")\n    \n    # Start with the edges that appear in both methods (more confident edges)\n    common_edges = list(set(pc_edges_filtered) & set(hc_edges_filtered))\n    print(f\"Common edges: {common_edges}\")\n    \n    # If we have less than 6 edges, add from either method\n    if len(common_edges) < 6:\n        # Add edges from PC then Hill Climbing until we reach 6\n        all_possible_edges = list(set(pc_edges_filtered + hc_edges_filtered))\n        # Remove duplicates and ensure U has no parents\n        all_possible_edges = [(u, v) for u, v in all_possible_edges if v != 'U']\n        # Prioritize edges with stronger relationships based on correlation\n        \n        # Create a list of edge strengths based on correlation\n        edge_strengths = []\n        for u, v in all_possible_edges:\n            strength = abs(corr_matrix.loc[u, v])\n            edge_strengths.append((u, v, strength))\n        \n        # Sort by strength\n        edge_strengths.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)\n        \n        # Select top 6 edges\n        final_edges = [(u, v) for u, v, _ in edge_strengths[:6]]\n    else:\n        # If we have more than 6, select the top 6 based on correlation\n        edge_strengths = []\n        for u, v in common_edges:\n            strength = abs(corr_matrix.loc[u, v])\n            edge_strengths.append((u, v, strength))\n        \n        edge_strengths.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)\n        final_edges = [(u, v) for u, v, _ in edge_strengths[:6]]\n\nprint(f\"Final edges: {final_edges}\")\nprint(f\"Number of edges: {len(final_edges)}\")\n\n# Double-check that U has no parents\nu_parents = [u for u, v in final_edges if v ==
